full_judgment:
Md Miftah Uddin Choudhury J: The appellant Md Sabuj Ahmed @ Ahmed Shamim Sabuj preferred this appeal under section 84 of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তি আইন, ২০০৬ (Act 39 at 2006) against the order dated 26-1-2017, passed by the Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka, in Cyber Tribunal Miscellaneous Petition Case No. 408 of 2016, rejecting his prayer for bail in GR Case No. 177 of 2016, corresponding to Mohammadpur Police Station Case No. 4 dated 10-9-2016, under section 57 of the said act pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Magura. 

 2. This appeal was admitted by order dated 13-3-2017. At the time of its admission an application for ad-interim bail was moved on behalf of the appellant. After hearing that application the learned Deputy Attorney General raised a question regarding jurisdiction of the Tribunal in entertaining the application for bail. As per him the case is still pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Magura and no police report has yet been submitted; that before submission of police report the tribunal cannot take cognizance, and before taking cognizance the Tribunal has got no authority to entertain any prayer for bail. 

 3. In reply of such question Mt Md Ruhul Quddus, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant replied, that the appellant was arrested by the police in connection with instant FIR lodged under section 57 of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তি আইন ২০০৬) on 15-11- 2016 and produced before the court of Chief Judicial Magistrate Magura who on rejection of prayer for bail by order dated 16-15-2016 remanded him to custody. Thereafter the appellant filed an application for bail before the Session Judge, Magura who refused to entertain that application and returned the same with the view that the bail prayer should be made before Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh), Dhaka. The said application for bail had not been registered as any Miscellaneous Case in that Court, but the application returned by the Session Judge has been annexed to the Supplementary Affidavit sworn on 12-3-2017 in supplement to the application filed for ad-interim bail and with that Affidavit a certificate issued by Mr Shafiqul Islam Shafique, a learned member of Magura Bar has also been annexed. As per that certificate the learned Advocate placed the application for bail before the Session Judge, Magura but the learned Judge refused to entertain it. 

 4. In such situation, we asked for explanation from the Session Judge, Magura about his refusal .to entertain the application for bail, and also from the Judge of Cyber Tribunal (Bangladesh) Dhaka about assuming his jurisdiction to entertain the application for bail when cognizance of the case has not been taken by the Tribunal. 

 6. The learned Session Judge, Magura named Mr Sheikh Mafizur Rahman by his memo No. 103/G dated .16-3-2017 sent his explanation stating that he was not in charge of Session Judge, Magura at the relevant time, rather he joined there on 13-3-2017. At the relevant time Begum Mahfuza Begum was Session Judge, Magura who is now retired. He talked to her over telephone and she said that before formation of the tribunal cognizance of such cases under said Act were taken and tried by Session Judges as a Session Case. As per the notification made in the Bangladesh Gazette, Extra issue dated 27th January 2013 a Cyber Tribunal has been set up in Dhaka having jurisdiction over entire Bangladesh. After its formation the tribunal will consider prayer for bail as per section 71 of the said Act (তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তি আইন, ২০০৬) and the Session Court is no more empowered to exercise its jurisdiction as provided in section 74 of the said Act. Hence, she did not entertain the prayer for bail. 

 7. From such explanation it appears that in fact the appellant filed an application for bail before the learned Session Judge, Magura but that was not entertained. The appellant was compelled to file an application for bail before the said Tribunal in Dhaka wherein it was registered as Cyber Tribunal Miscellaneous Petition Case No. 408 of 2016. 

 (5) Moreover, a Bench of the High Court division composed of their lordships Mr Justice Md Nizamul Haque and Mr Justice AKM Zahirul Haque, in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 12763 of 2015 and 12582 of 2013 directed the accused to surrender before the Cyber Tribunal and also directed the Tribunal to hear and decide the prayer for bail. Similarly another Bench composed of their lordship Mr Justice Md Rezaul Haque and Mr 	Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 35359 of 2014 	and 34599 of 2014 directed the accused to surrender before the Tribunal and also directed 	the Tribunal to dispose up the bail prayer. 

 (6) The Miscellaneous petition case was heard and decided by his predecessor; 

 1(a) Order dated 6-4-2015 passed in Criminal' Miscellaneous Case No.12763 of 2015 by a Division Bench of this Court Division composed of their lordships Mr. Justice Md. Nizarnul Haque and Mr justice AKM Zahirul Haque, 

 1(b) and subsequent Order dated 29-4-2015 passed in said' Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.12763 of 2015 by another division bench composed of their lordships Mr Justice Md Qumrul Islam Siddique and Mr Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore. 

 2(a) Order dated 6-4-2015 passed by a Division Bench of this Court composed of their lordships Mr Justice Md Nizamul Haque and Mr Justice AKM Zahirul Haque in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12582 of 2015. 

 2(b) and subsequent Order dated 29-4-2015 passed in the said Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12582 of 2015 by another division Bench composed of their lordships Mr Justice Quamrul Islam Siddiqui and Mr Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore. 

 3. Order dated 2-9-2014 passed by another division bench of this Court composed of Mr Justice Rezaul Haque and Mr. Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No 34599 of 2014 

 4. and Order dated 9-9-2014 passed by the same Bench composed of same Honorable Judges in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 35359 of 2014. 

 11. On perusal of the order dated 6-4-2015 and 29-42015 passed by two different Bench in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12763 of 2015 it appears that the Division Bench composed of their lordships Mr Justice Md Nizamul Haq and Mr Justice AMM Zahirul Haq by Order dated 6-4-2015 without issuing any Rule granted anticipatory bail to accused petitioner for a period of 4 (four) weeks on furnishing bail bond to the satisfaction of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and directed the accused to surrender before the same court at the end of such period and by the same order the application filed for anticipatory bail was disposed of. But before acceptance of the bail bond the case record was transferred to the Tribunal and cognizance was, taken therein for which the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate refused to accept the bail bond. In such circumstances the accused prayed for correction in the said order directing the Tribunal to accept the bail bond: and the Accused to surrender before the Tribunal. Accordingly the other bench composed of their lordships Mr Justice Quamrul Islam Siddique and Mr Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore by subsequent order dated 29-4-2015 allowed to make correction 'in the previous order. Apparently the correction was made in the order dated 6-4-2015 by penning through the words "Chief Judicial Magistrate" and inserting the words "Cyber Crime Tribunal". 

 12. On perusal of the orders dated 6-4-2015 and 29-4-2015 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12582 of 2015 by two different Benches composed same Honorable Judges it appears that similar orders were passed in similar circumstance, and similar correction was made in similar manner. 

 13. On perusal of the order dated 2-9-2014 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 34599 of 2014 by another Division Bench composed of their lordships Mr Justice Md Rezaul Haq and Mr Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore it appears that the accused surrendered with an application for anticipatory bail on the plea that the Tribunal is authorized to deal with their bail prayer under section 71 of the Information and Communication Technology Act, 2006 (তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তি আইন ২০০৬, but the record is lying with the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka and they have no forum to surrender. Their lordships without granting anticipatory bail prayed by the accused directed the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka to transmit the case record immediately to the Tribunal and directed the accused to surrender before the Tribunal with in 2 (two) weeks. 

 14. On perusal of the order dated 9-9-2014 passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 35359 of 2014 by the same bench composed of same Honorable judges it appears the petitioner of that case took same plea and their lordships without granting anticipatory bail directed the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka to transmit the record immediately to the Tribunal and directed the accused petitioner to surrender before the Tribunal within 2 (two) weeks, and also directed the law enforcing agencies not to arrest or harass the accused petitioner during that period'. 

 15. On perusal of the aforesaid two orders passed in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 34599 of 2014 and 35359 of 2014 by the Division Bench composed of their lordships, Mr Justice Md Rezaul Haq and Mr Justice Gobinda Chandra Tagore it appears that such orders were obtained by misleading the court on misinterpretation of section 71 of the said Act. 

 19. In the instant case we find no such report or approval. 

 24. As per section 70(1) of the said Act, in proceeding with trial of a case under said act the Tribunal is authorized to exercise all powers of the Session Court as its original jurisdiction. It is apparent that the Tribunal is not yet in seisin of the case since no cognizance was taken and no case record is available before it. Moreover, the Session Judge does not hear any application for bail in, a case, pending in the court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate/Chief Judicial Magistrate or any other subordinate court in its original jurisdiction. The Session Judge hears the same as Miscellaneous Jurisdiction like the High Court Division under 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 25. The said Act does not provide any provision that for mere registration of an FIR under any section of the' said Act. The Magistrate or Sessions Judge or High Court Division cannot hear the prayer for bail when cognizance has not been taken by the tribunal and while the case is under investigation. Before taking cognizance the Tribunal cannot assume its power to hear the prayer for bail. 

 26. It is apparent that, in the instant case no police report has yet been submitted or no prior approval was given by the controller or any officer authorized by him for such purpose. As such the Tribunal cannot and did not take cognizance of the case. And before taking cognizance hearing of bail prayer made in any case under said act cannot treated as legal for want of jurisdiction. 

 28. We hold the view that only for mere registration of an FIR alleging any offence under a particular law which is triable by any Tribunal before taking cognizance of the case or when the case is under investigation such Tribunal cannot assume its jurisdiction to entertain prayer for bail. We hold further that before submission of the police report and before taking cognizance such tribunal cannot entertain any prayer for bail as it done in the instant case. Our such view got support from the decision of this court reported in 17 BLT 192. 

 29. The instant case is still under investigation and as such the Tribunal has got no jurisdiction to entertain such application. 

 31. The learned Judge further mentioned about one order passed by a Division Bench composed of their lordships Mr Justice Md Nizamul Haq and AKM Zahirul Haque in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 12582 of 2013. We bring the record of the said case from record room and on perusal it appears that the order/judgment in that case was passed by another Bench composed of his lordship Mr Justice M. Enayetur Rahim and Mr Justice Amir Hossain. 

 32. When the High Court Division asked about jurisdiction of his court to entertain a petition he ought to be cautious in giving reply, but we are/hopeless to find that he mentioned a wrong number of a case in his explanation. 

 40. However, his prayer for bail placed before this Court. Section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure does not provide that only on an application mentioning that section the High Court can consider prayer for bail. We hold the view that without mentioning any section of any law an accused during trial, investigation, or inquiry of a case can approach this court for bail.
